steps.title: A pool deep enough
steps.body: Water deeper than about half the hero's height is swum, not waded. A Pool from the dock is 3 studs deep: plenty.
steps.task: In the dock, open Water and press Place beside Pool (or right-click the ground: Add water here).

how.text: Click “Scene” in the workspace tabs, then in the dock at the bottom open Water and place a Pool.

steps.title: Treasure at the bottom
steps.body: Something worth diving for: a Treasure chest on the pool's floor.
steps.task: Place a Treasure chest inside the pool (Dock › Assets › Treasure chest, then click the pool's floor).

how.text: Pick the Treasure chest in the dock and click in the middle of the pool.

do.say: The chest sits on the pool's floor.

steps.title: How long a breath lasts
steps.body: Project › Swimming: with Hero can swim on, the hero floats in deep water and can dive. Breath is how many seconds of air the hero has under water; with none left a heart is lost every 2 seconds.
steps.task: On the Project tab, set Breath to 30 seconds.

how.text: On the right, click the Project tab.

steps.title: Dive
steps.body: Press Play and walk into the pool: the hero floats and the Action button in the corner says Dive. Hold E to go down. Under water the view turns blue, the Air bar counts down, and the button says Swim up. Let go and the hero drifts back up.
steps.task: Press Play, swim into the pool and hold E to dive under.

steps.title: Open it under water
steps.body: The Action button always does what fits: by the chest it says Open, even under water (opening wins over swimming up).
steps.task: Swim down to the chest's front and press E.

steps.title: Done!
steps.body: You made a pool, hid a chest at the bottom, set how long a breath lasts, dived and opened the chest under water. Jump at the surface or swim into a low shore to climb out; a river's current carries swimmers. Help › Swimming and Controls say more, and Project › Controls picks the game's button layout.
